notes:
Identity verified from supplied title FORMING IMPRESSIONS OF PERSONALITY, author S. E. ASCH, DOI header 10.1037/h0055756. Every assigned description identifies Experiment I but leaves the individual secondary-quality outcome unspecified. No audit ID assigned to a table row by order or numeric matching. Candidate Experiment I percentages, warm/cold: generous: 91/8; wise: 65/25; happy: 90/34; good-natured: 94/17; humorous: 77/13; sociable: 91/38; popular: 84/28; reliable: 94/99; important: 88/99; humane: 86/31; good-looking: 77/69; persistent: IOO/97; serious: IOO/99; restrained: 77/89; altruistic: 69/18; imaginative: 51/19; strong: 98/95; honest: 98/94. IOO is preserved as canonical OCR, not silently corrected. Percentages are not ORs; no effect-size conversion. Candidate experiment group membership: 90 + 76 = 166 participants, across 4 + 4 = 8 classrooms; classroom and participant roles are distinct. This is not an established item-specific analytic N, because omitted answers and varying denominators are explicitly reported, especially good-looking/unattractive. Exact item omissions/exclusions are not enumerated; no analytic N sum extracted. Experiment I results on pp. 262–265 and Table 2 provide percentages and narrative comparisons, with no numerical same-test p. No source PDF path supplied; no render.
